theory.en: an idea or explanation that is proposed to account for something

evidence.en: facts or signs that show something is true

constant.en: a value or quantity that does not change

experiment.en: a scientific test done to learn or prove something

sample.en: a small part taken from something to study it

instrument.en: a tool or device used for measuring or scientific work

interval.en: a period of time or space between two things

measurement.en: the size or amount found by measuring

hypothesis.en: an idea that is suggested as a possible explanation and then tested

artifact.en: an object made by people, especially one of historical interest

habitat.en: the natural home of an animal or plant

specimen.en: an example of a plant, animal, etc. kept for study

prediction.en: a statement about what will happen or is true before it is checked

boundary.en: a line that marks the edge of an area

claim.en: a statement that something is true

temperature.en: how hot or cold something is

survey.en: a set of questions asked to gather information

exception.en: something that does not follow the usual rule

device.en: a machine or tool made for a purpose

projection.en: an estimate of what will happen in the future

plain.en: simple and without decoration; easy to understand

lucid.en: clear and easy to see through (of air or water)

limpid.en: completely clear and easy to see through

familiar.en: well known because seen or heard often

rectify.en: to correct or fix something that is wrong

display.en: to show something so people can see it

remedy.en: to fix or solve a problem

advertise.en: to tell the public about something to promote it

preserve.en: to keep something in its original state

intensify.en: to make something stronger or more extreme

redress.en: to correct something unfair or wrong

describe.en: to say what something is like

continue.en: to keep doing or keep happening

summarize.en: to give the main points briefly

alleviate.en: to make a problem or pain less severe

promote.en: to help something grow or become popular

correct.en: to make something right or fix an error

extend.en: to make something longer or larger

circumvent.en: to find a way around a rule or obstacle

corroborate.en: to support or confirm with evidence

implement.en: to put a plan or decision into action

avoid.en: to keep away from or stop something from happening

apply.en: to use something in a particular situation

support.en: to show that an idea or result is true

publish.en: to make information available to the public

confirm.en: to show that something is true or correct

distribute.en: to give or share out among many people

perform.en: to do or carry out an action

evade.en: to avoid or escape from something

substantiate.en: to provide evidence that proves something

validate.en: to show that something is true or correct

spread.en: to cause to reach a wider area or more people

bypass.en: to go around something to avoid it

execute.en: to carry out a plan or action

verify.en: to check that something is true

circulate.en: to pass from person to person

demarcated from.en: clearly separated or set apart from
demarcated from.zh: 與……區分開來；與……劃清界線

reconstituted as.en: formed again in a different way as

conflated with.en: wrongly treated as the same as

distinguish.en: to show or recognize a difference between things

confuse.en: to mistake one thing for another

derive.en: to get or develop something from a source

derived.en: obtained or developed from a source

copied.en: made something the same as something else

differentiated.en: showed or made a difference between

distinguished.en: recognized or showed the difference between
